messages:
alex: Heads-up — rolled a container rebuild in us-west-2 canaries at 04:12 and ~30% of GPU nodes in the canary pool are crashing at runtime. NCCL init failures + python workers SIGABRT. Logs below.
ops-bot: deploybot: image rebuild ff/toolchain-2026-03-05 completed by jamie at 2026-03-05T04:12:00Z
jamie: I kicked the rebuild, CI was green. sorry — paste logs pls.
alex: here are the key snippets:
```
2026-03-05T04:20:12.123Z worker[2387]: RuntimeError: cuda runtime error (78) : no kernel image is available for execution
python[2387]: fatal error: init: undefined symbol: _ZTVN10__cxxabiv117__class_type_infoE
NCCL WARN: unexpected error during init - errno 22
```
maria: That "undefined symbol" looks like a libstdc++/ABI mismatch. Image was built with gcc13 on toolkit12 base; a bunch of hosts still have older system libstdc++ and driver stack.
ryan: Confirming on a flapping node: `nvidia-smi` reports Driver Version: 525.85.12, CUDA Version: 11.8.
lisa: How widespread is it? only canary nodes or did autoscaler pull prod into the same config?
alex: Canary first, but autoscaler accidentally pulled some prod backfills into the same config — we have 8 prod GPU nodes flapping now. Seeing capacity pressure and 503s on chat endpoints.
jamie: We built images with base: `redwood/toolkit:12-gcc13-2026-03` to pick up performance fixes. I didn't run a cross-driver smoke matrix, my bad.
maria: Short term options: revert to previous image tag `toolkit:11.8-gcc9` or rebuild the toolkit12 images with an ABI compatibility shim. Rebuilding with `-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0` might help but can break wheels compiled against the new ABI.
ryan: Ops asks: can we pin staging nodes to driver 535 to validate toolkit12 images? Fleet-wide driver upgrade is heavy and requires kernel module DKMS builds.
lisa: Cost / routing note — if we fail over traffic to Dedicated capacity or other regions to maintain SLAs, it could be ~3x cost. Avoid cross-region failover unless needed.
ops-bot: incident-bot: created INC-2026-1035 (P2) — assigned to eng-infra & eng-runtime.
alex: Temporary mitigation: cordon the affected nodes, and roll a revert to previous image for the canary pool. I'll open a rollout and freeze further rebuilds.
jamie: I'm rebuilding hotfix images now with libstdc++ compatibility bits and adding an entrypoint runtime check. Example check I'm adding:
```
# at container entry
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,cuda_version --format=csv
strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 | grep GLIBCXX || true
```
maria: Postmortem actions: add matrixed CI: build/test images against oldest supported driver and newest driver, add preflight smoke test on canary nodes for "no kernel image" error, and require a manual sign-off when toolchain changes.
ryan: Runbook suggestion for nodes: host bootstrap should assert libstdc++ symbols early: `if ! strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6 | grep GLIBCXX_3.4.30; then echo 'abi-old' && exit 1; fi` so we don't join mismatched hosts to the GPU pool.
lisa: Looping in finance: @finance-team FYI — we might need emergency budget for Dedicated spillover.
alex: TL;DR — cause = images compiled with gcc13/toolkit12 mismatching driver + libstdc++ on some hosts after rebuild. Plan = revert image + rebuild with compatibility OR pin toolchain + add CI matrix + host preflight + plan driver upgrade roadmap. Updating incident and running revert now.
